summary: Ta~Al!N~C! thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with TaCl5 or TaBr5 and NH3 as precursors, and trimethylaluminum (TMA) as an additional reducing agent. The films were analyzed for composition, resistivity, and barrier properties. The deposition temperature significantly affected the film properties, with the best results obtained at 400°C.
evidence: Ta~Al!N~C! thin films were deposited by the atomic layer deposition technique using TaCl5 or TaBr5 and NH3 as precursors and Al(CH3)3 as an additional reducing agent. The deposition temperature was varied between 250 and 400°C. The film deposited at 400°C contained less than 4 atom % chlorine and also had the lowest resistivity, 1300 mV cm. The barrier properties of the Cu/Ta~Al!N~C!/Si structure were studied by using sheet resistance and X-ray diffraction measurements.
